utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the Registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-02-65-PT, the Prosecutor versus Zeljko Meakic, Momcilo Gruban, Dusan Fustar, Predrag Banovic, and Dusko Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I have the appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: If the Court pleases, I appear for the Prosecution, my name is Sureta Chana. I am ably assisted by my learned counsel here, Katharina Margetts, and our case manager today is David Leese.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Chana. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCUDDER
utterances.text: I am Theodore Scudder, representing Dusan Fustar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Scudder. Is there a problem with the microphone? Why don't you use the microphone that is working.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am Tom Moran. I am co-counsel for Mr. Knezevic, and I am with lead counsel, Slobodanka Nedic, from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Moran.

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Jovan Babic, I am a lawyer from Novi Sad, and I am representing Predrag Banovic here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Babic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUNDJER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Milenko Dundjer, and I shall be representing Momcilo Gruban today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dundjer. We have a number of matters to consider in this status conference, but the one I want to deal with first is the pleas to the new charges that arise out of the consolidated indictment. Mr. Gruban and Mr. Knezevic will plead to new charges. And before I move into the formal process of taking their pleas, I want to be sure that we have a common understanding as to the new charges to which they will be pleading. So I ask counsel, listen carefully as I read out the charges. In respect of Mr. Knezevic, the new charges are count 4, inhumane acts, a crime against humanity; and count 5, cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war. And in respect of Mr. Gruban, the new charges are inhumane acts, a crime against humanity; cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war; and persecution, a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5, 7(1), and 7(3) of this Statute. So I would just like to have that confirmed by counsel on both sides that those are the new charges. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm those are the new charges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And for the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Dundjer? Yes, thank you. So Mr. Dundjer, Ms. Nedic, and Mr. Moran, as defence counsel, I take it that your clients have received copies of the consolidated indictment in a language which they understand and that you have had the opportunity of going through it about them and that you have brought to their attention the new charges that they face and that you have explained the charges to them. First Mr. Dundjer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUNDJER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have received the indictment. We have informed the accused of this matter. Everything was explained to him, and the matter is clear to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Nedic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We have explained to the accused Knezevic all the counts that concern him in the consolidated indictment, and he understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Gruban, please stand. You've heard your counsel say that the indictment has been explained to you. He has informed you of the nature of the new charges against you. And do you wish to enter a plea to those charges today? THE ACCUSED GRUBAN: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to read the new counts in the indictment. And to each count, you will enter a plea, and you will say either guilty or not guilty. Count 1 of the consolidated indictment charges you with persecution on political, racial, or religious grounds, a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5, 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED GRUBAN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And count 4 charges you with inhumane acts, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(1), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED GRUBAN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Count 5 charges you with cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) 12 of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 and punishable under Articles 3,7(1) and 13 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED GRUBAN: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. Mr. Knezevic, please stand. You've heard what your counsel has said. The indictment has been read to you in a language that you understand, and he has been through the indictment with you, explained the new charges to you. Do you wish to enter a plea to those new charges today? THE ACCUSED KNEZEVIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I will put the charges to you, and you will answer guilty or not guilty. Count 4 of the consolidated indictment charges you with inhumane acts, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(1), and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED KNEZEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And count 5 charges you with cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 and punishable under Article 3, and Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED KNEZEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit. Let us now proceed to the other matters that we have to consider and decide at this Pre-Trial Conference. I will go through the list of matters that I have, and I will call on counsel as the occasion arises. First, pre-trial motions: Defence...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm consulting with the Registrar. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Registrar is consulting the transcript. I will proceed, and when that matter is resolved, the matter I am discussing with the Registrar, we'll come back to it at a later stage. Pre-trial motions, Defence preliminary motions, are to be filed by the 23rd of December. The Prosecution has already indicated it will need Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. some more time to put in its response. And I understand one or two weeks would be enough. I will give two weeks, until Monday, January the 6th, for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may speak now, Ms. Korner had asked for two weeks' extension. We would actually, at this stage, ask you to the 27th of January, if we may, to file our response to any motion filed by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's more than two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: It is just because of the holiday season, Your Honour, and the staff will be sort of coming back. We would be prepared to -- I mean, it was January 3rd we should have filed by. 6th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'll grant that extension, then. To January the --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: The 27th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: 27th.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Prosecution motion for protective measures that was filed on the 4th of December, and the Defence responses are due on the 18th of December. I just make that point as a reminder. We come now to the pre-trial briefs. At the last conference, I had set a target of two months from the decision on joinder for the filing of the Prosecution brief, and the Defence briefs to come a month later. The joinder decision was issued on the 17th of December [sic], but the consolidated indictment was only accepted on the 21st of November. So what I am going to do is to set the pre-trial brief for the Prosecution to be submitted by Friday, February the 7th. And for all the defendants, including Knezevic, and I take into account the new counsel, March the 31st for their brief. I move now to disclosure. I see Ms. Chana wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, before we leave the pre-trial brief, Your Honour, we were wondering whether we could have a page extension. We are limited to 50 pages as of now, and there are four accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: We would like to address in our pre-trial brief, it would make it easier also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What are you requesting?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: We are requesting 120 pages, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'll grant that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On the question of disclosure, the witness statements under Rule 66(A)(i) all statements that accompany the indictment, the original indictment or, indeed, the consolidated indictment, have now been disclosed in both English and B/C/S. And with regard to Rule 66(A)(ii), statements of most of the witnesses to be called have been disclosed under 66(A)(i), and I understand the only remaining disclosure would relate to any additional witnesses that the Prosecution may identify when it finalises its witness list. And as for the Prosecution witness list, I would set the same date for the submission of that list as for the pre-trial brief. That's February the 7th. No question of reciprocal disclosure has been invoked. Rule 68 material, my information is that the Prosecution is still conducting the necessary searches and will disclose any material as it finds it. Experts, we had been given to understand that the Prosecution would call five experts, but it now appears, from the 65 ter conference, that only one, Mr. Sebire, has been identified. I'll ask the Prosecutor to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Sebire has been identified, but we've already disclosed three other expert witnesses when we had the Keraterm part of the case, which is Hannah Greaves, Richard Wright and Dr. John Clark. And Mr. Sebire would be in addition to those three, so we are looking at four, possibly five, expert witnesses at this time, Your Honour, three of which have been disclosed, but not to all the counsels, I believe, not the ones with the joinder, but we will disclose to them as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: For that disclosure, I would set the date of Friday, January the 24th.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And we also have to set a date for the submission of the exhibit lists by the Prosecution. And I set that date as Friday, February the 7th. Agreed facts. The Prosecution has prepared a list of facts for possible agreement. And the list of findings from previous judgements. These have been provided to the Defence, and the parties are to meet to discuss this matter and come to an agreement, if that is possible. I encourage the parties to do that as quickly as possible. The length of trial. Ms. Chana, can you remind me of the number of witnesses that you expect to call.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: We anticipate 50 witnesses in all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: 50 witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Live witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And the length of your case?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, it all depends on what the agreed facts are. If there are, in fact -- if there is an agreement on a lot of the background facts, of course, it would only leave us with the individual criminal responsibility which will severely curtail our case. In that event, we're probably looking at six to eight weeks to finish our Prosecution case. In the event that we do not have many facts on which we reach agreement, then I anticipate at least six months, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I encourage the parties to come to agreement, if that is possible, and shorten the case. I am required to make an inquiry from each of the accused as to any matter which they wish to raise concerning their detention, conditions relating to their detention or to their health. Before I do that, counsel wishes to say something. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I presume that my defendant will also wish to speak on this issue, but we wanted to raise the matter that -- the problem that he has in the Detention Unit at the moment, which is the following: The basis for the submission is to be found at Rule 65 bis (A)(ii), and this is to do with the mental state of my client in the Detention Unit. On the 13th of June of this year, in the usual way, I addressed the Registry for the Registry to undertake certain steps in respect of the authorities of the Netherlands so that the visa can be issued to Nenad Banovic, brother of Predrag Banovic, for the purpose of a visit. The response from the Registry following this request, I received in July. The response was a negative one. The reason was very brief in the written response, and they were given -- the reasons given was security reasons. These didn't seem very convincing reasons, and at my next meeting with Mr. Christian Rhode, I discussed this matter. And the agreement that came out of that meeting was for me to address the Registry again. I did so on the 18th of September in the same manner with a slightly expanded explanation. On the 27th of November, I received practically the same answer, that steps cannot be taken in respect of the Dutch authorities, and that the Registry believes that this visa cannot be issued for security purposes in relation to the Detention Unit. Both these decisions, and particularly the latter, have caused my client, Predrag Banovic, to be mentally unstable. His concentration on the preparation of his Defence has been decreasing on a daily basis. And particularly, he is hurt by the fact that his brother, his twin brother, through a very rough identification error, and we, as the Defence, will seriously address this problem of identification in our preliminary Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. motion, this brother had been brought before this Tribunal. He spent a certain amount of time in the Detention Unit of the Tribunal, then the indictment was withdrawn against him; the Tribunal dismissed the case against him, and he is currently free. It seems that the father, the mother, brother, second brother, his wife can visit him here in the Detention Unit, while his twin brother, where special emotional links exist and only as a result of a serious identification error, he cannot be given a visa for a visit to the Detention Unit. I believe that Your Honour and this Chamber would be authorised in this manner to order the Registry for -- so that the Registry attempts, does its utmost, so the Registry can make sure that Nenad Banovic is issued with a visa to visit his brother. That way, the mental state of Predrag Banovic, my client, will be stabilised and make him able to stand trial. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Babic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, I've listened to what you have said very carefully, and I understand it is a distressing matter for your client. I'm not sure, however, to what extent the Chamber is in a position to deal with this effectively. I will, however, ask the Registrar to have the matter investigated, and anything that can be done, I would expect that it will be done. In the meantime, if your client is not well, perhaps you would see to it that he receives appropriate medical attention and make appropriate representations to that end. Because I understand you to be saying that his mental condition is not good and is deteriorating as a result of his not being able to see his twin brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, you have understood me well. And that's what I brought up. And one of the measures taken this morning is that I have asked a psychologist who regularly visits the detainees to speak to my client and to pay particular attention to him, to follow him for a while, until a decision has been reached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. In the meantime, I'll ask the Registrar to ensure that the matter is kept under review. Is there anything else to be raised by any other counsel? Mr. Dundjer?

utterances.speaker: MR. BABIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I had one other question to raise here, one other issue, which is the following: Again, I believe that this is in connection with all the accused, but of course I am speaking on behalf of my client. The material that we received yesterday, or in the last few days, from the Prosecution about the uncontested facts or the tried facts, we received this material in English. The material is about 50 pages long. At the meeting with Ms. Featherstone, we asked for this material to be translated for this reason: This material has to be read by the accused. My client doesn't speak English. He doesn't speak any language -- official language of the Tribunal. I believe that he has a right to receive material in his own language, the language that he understands so that the next meeting with me he can discuss this material. In this way, we will make sure that this trial proceeds in a more efficient and swift manner. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I ask the Prosecutor to respond to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. This matter had been brought up at the 65 ter conference, Your Honour, where Ms. Featherstone had volunteered that the Registry would assist in giving transcripts in B/C/S. And I believe it is not the Prosecutor's duty to provide this material since it is in the public domain in B/C/S. We provided it in English, and I suggest counsel avail themselves of Ms. Featherstone's offer of assisting if they can't find the B/C/S transcripts and the tapes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Senior legal officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand that consultations are taking place to facilitate a translation. This appears to relate more to a matter of the facility of counsel to work in the working languages of the Tribunal. But nonetheless, everything that can be done by the Chamber through the senior legal officer will be done. Mr. Dundjer, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUNDJER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of Momcilo Gruban asked certain questions at the conference, and they can be summed up in the following: We received the statements of Prosecution witnesses. I don't want to discuss witnesses further, but I'd just like to raise the most important matters. We did not receive complete statements, and I have already listed which witnesses they are as examples. And what I request is for this matter to be taken into consideration. Then regarding the disclosure of exculpatory material in accordance with Rule 68, the Defence of Momcilo Gruban does know that at the Status Conference of Kvocka and the others, which is held -- which was held about a month ago, what was mentioned is that there were over 50.000 pages of documents. Not all of them, but they are all exculpatory. Since this is a case which is very closely connected to this case, what I request is that the Defence in this case, too, can obtain this exculpatory material which is in relation to the other case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will you just explain, Mr. Dundjer, what you meant when you said that the witness statements were not complete. I didn't quite understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUNDJER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I said was that we received one statement. While these witnesses gave several statements, and they have also testified in other cases before this Tribunal - for instance, in the Stakic case - for instance, one witness testified in several instances, in Stakic case, the Brdjanin case and so on, at in the conference I said Azedin Oklopcic, Suada Ramic, Asim Baltic, et cetera, all of these witnesses have testified and have given several statements, although we only received one statement. That's the question that I wanted to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, while we have made very good progress in our disclosure, we have not as yet disclosed everything. And we will be, in due course, providing counsel with all the additional statements any particular witness made. We have disclosed everything in respect of our original and supporting material obligations, but we still have some outstanding disclosure that we are at the moment doing, and we will provide counsel. We had also made an offer to counsel at the 65 ter conference that if he would put in writing to us any particular statements which he thinks he ought to have, we would be very happy to also look into that and hand them over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, that seems to be a very practical proposal. So put what you want in writing. Any other counsel wishing to make any statement at this stage? If not, then I'll go to the four accused, starting with Mr. Knezevic. Mr. Knezevic, do you have anything that you want to raise in relation to your conditions of detention or your health? THE ACCUSED KNEZEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have nothing to say. Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Gruban. THE ACCUSED GRUBAN: [Interpretation] I have no observations to make. I have no complaints.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Banovic, we already heard your counsel, but if you want to reiterate what he has said, then you may do so. THE ACCUSED BANOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I wanted to say is that I stand by what my Defence attorney said. My health will be much better, will be much improved, once my brother has had his visa approved. Because of this unfortunate incident that he was indicted, that he had been indicted and that he had spent time in this Detention Unit, I believe that neither I should suffer the consequences nor should he. The fact that by a mistake he spent four or five months in detention, I believe that both our human rights are being violated, his and mine. And I absolutely do not understand the decision of the Registry to give us just this very summary answer that his security does not allow him to visit him [as interpreted]. We are identical twins, and this is the first time that we have been separated for such a long time. Perhaps it's a very difficult thing to understand for you. Very few people can understand this, only people who have twin brothers or sisters can understand this. He is the person that understands me the best, and that's why I am requesting that really I will be much improved if he is issued with a visa to visit me from time to time, because I am certain that the approval of this visa will influence the further proceedings and even the case, my case, in this case and in this trial. Thank you very much in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Banovic. As I said to your counsel, while recognising that security matters are essentially matters for the Detention Unit, through the Registrar, I'm going to encourage that this matter be looked into and see to what extent your concerns can be accommodated. Mr. Fustar. THE ACCUSED FUSTAR: [Interpretation] I have nothing to say in relation to the Detention Unit. I'm satisfied. We're being professionally treated. And that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fustar. The date of the next Status Conference will be Tuesday, the 8th of April. A matter has been raised as to whether all the new counts to which the two accused were pleaded were actually put. And for that purpose, for that reason, I am going to adjourn for 15 minutes to have this checked properly. In the meantime, I'll ask both counsel involved to investigate the matter. And we'll resume in 15 minutes. --- Break taken at 3.52 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In the adjournment, it was determined that one count had not been put to Mr. Knezevic. It is count 1, which charges him with persecution. I just want to have it confirmed by Ms. Nedic for Mr. Knezevic that this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. In the earlier two cases, in one of the indictments there was a count for persecution, and that concerns Keraterm. But that count did not exist for Omarska in the indictment so it was added to the consolidated indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And you've had a chance to explain this to Mr. Knezevic, that I'm now going to put this count to him?

utterances.speaker: MS. NEDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have had the opportunity of explaining this to him during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Nedic. Mr. Knezevic, please stand. It has been explained to you that count 1 was not put to you, and I'm now going to put it to you. Count 1 charges you with persecution on political, racial, or religious grounds, a crime against humanity under Article 5 and 7(1) of the Statute. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED KNEZEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit. There being no other matter, the hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: [Trial Chamber and senior legal officer confer]
[Trial Chamber and the senior legal officer confer]
